2306.content:
The support vector perspective describes an SVM solution through the training observations that lie on or inside its margin. Cases farther from the boundary receive zero weight in the dual representation.

Because the decision function depends on this subset, support vectors summarize the boundary-relevant evidence. Their number affects prediction cost and reveals how much of the training set remains necessary after optimization.

2309.title: Support Vector Machine Dual Problem
2309.heading: Support Vector Machine Dual Problem
2309.content:
The support vector machine dual problem rewrites margin optimization in terms of one coefficient for each training observation. Feature vectors appear only through pairwise inner products, which permits kernel substitution.

Box and equality constraints restrict the coefficients, and observations with nonzero solutions become support vectors. The dual can be advantageous when feature dimension is large, though its quadratic dependence on training cases creates scaling challenges.

2312.title: Support Team
2312.heading: Support Team
2312.content:
A support team supplies a capability used by many development teams, such as build infrastructure or specialized services. Its work often arrives continuously from multiple requesters and is well suited to visible flow policies.

The team needs a clear service boundary and ordering mechanism. Without them, urgent requests and hidden dependencies fragment attention and turn the team into a bottleneck.

2315.title: Support of a Module
2315.heading: Support of a Module
2315.content:
The support Supp(M) of an R-module is the set of prime ideals p for which the localization M_p is nonzero. It identifies where the module remains visible on the ring's spectrum.

For a finitely generated module, support consists exactly of primes containing Ann(M). Every [[Associated Prime]] belongs to the support, and every support prime contains an associated prime.

2318.title: Support Count
2318.heading: Support Count
2318.content:
Support count is the number of transactions that contain a specified itemset. It is the raw frequency underlying both itemset support and association-rule evaluation.

Candidate generation methods use support counts to discard combinations that occur too rarely. Counting normally requires scanning the transaction data or maintaining an equivalent summary.

2321.heading: Supplementary Elements in Correspondence Analysis
2321.content:
A supplementary element is projected into an existing correspondence-analysis factor space without defining its principal axes. This permits a study to use coarse categories as the active table while retaining finer attributes for interpretation.

The book calls this information focusing: aggregate observations or attributes establish a lower-resolution geometry, and the full detail can then be mapped into it. The approach can reduce computational and interpretive load, but the chosen active resolution remains a substantive modeling decision.

Status: #baby

Tags: [[Neural Network Training]], [[Parallel Neural Network Training]]

2324.title: Supervised Learning
2324.heading: Supervised Learning
2324.content:
Supervised learning trains a model from examples paired with desired outputs. The model adjusts its parameters to reduce the difference between its prediction and the supplied label.

Speech transcriptions, intent labels, and marked entity spans can provide supervision for assistant components. The method depends on a representative [[Training Dataset]], and producing reliable labels can be expensive.

For classification, every training observation is paired with a [[Class Label]]. A neural network produces an initial prediction, measures it with a [[Loss Function]], and changes its parameters so later predictions better match the supplied targets. A [[Test Dataset]] that did not participate in these updates evaluates whether the learned relationship generalizes.

Kelleher emphasizes that target labels give the learner direct feedback on how a candidate function performed. Creating those labels can be costly, especially for large image datasets that need expert or human annotation. The feedback helps guide optimization, but labeled data still must represent the cases on which the model will later be used.

2326.sourceSearchName: supervised distance metric learning supervised distance metric learning
2326.title: Supervised Distance Metric Learning
2326.heading: Document

2327.sourceSearchName: supervised distance metric learning supervised distance metric learning
2327.title: Supervised Distance Metric Learning
2327.heading: Supervised Distance Metric Learning
2327.content:
Supervised distance metric learning uses class labels or must-link and cannot-link pairs to shape a distance function. Same-label or must-linked observations should be close, while conflicting labels or cannot-links should be separated.

Methods differ in whether the transformation is linear or nonlinear, global or local, and inductive or transductive. These choices determine whether the learned metric can be applied to new cases and whether it preserves neighborhood distinctions throughout the space.

2328.title: Supervised Distance Metric Learning
2328.heading: References

2330.title: Supervised Classification
2330.heading: Supervised Classification
2330.content:
Supervised classification learns from records whose class labels are known. The training data provide examples of the relationship between attributes and the target category.

A complete workflow constructs the model, evaluates it on separate or withheld cases, and applies it to unseen records. The evaluation estimates whether the learned relationship generalizes.

2332.sourceSearchName: superposed time series plot superposed time series plot
2332.title: Superposed Time-Series Plot
2332.heading: Document

2333.sourceSearchName: superposed time series plot superposed time series plot
2333.title: Superposed Time-Series Plot
2333.heading: Superposed Time-Series Plot
2333.content: A superposed time-series plot draws several comparable series in one panel against a shared time axis and value scale. It reveals collective motion and departures from the group, but many opaque lines quickly become unreadable. Thin strokes and [[Transparency for Time-Series Overplotting]] can shift attention from individual paths to density. Superposition is appropriate only when the variables share units or have been transformed into a common comparison scale.

2334.title: Superposed Time-Series Plot
2334.heading: References

2336.title: Summative Evaluation
2336.heading: Summative Evaluation
2336.content:
Summative evaluation assesses a substantially complete interface against target values or compares two or more designs, components, or techniques. It helps sum up the quality and consequences of design choices.

Representative users perform consistent task scenarios while evaluators collect qualitative and quantitative results. Formal summative experiments vary independent variables, measure dependent variables, and control other factors so observed effects can be attributed to the design conditions.

Summative evaluation complements [[Formative Evaluation]]. Formative work refines the design; summative work measures the resulting design or compares alternatives.

2338.title: Superintelligence
2338.heading: Document

Status: #baby

Tags: [[AI Futures and Human Identity]]

2339.title: Superintelligence
2339.heading: Superintelligence
2339.content:
Superintelligence is a hypothetical form of artificial intelligence that exceeds human cognitive ability across most important domains. It is often imagined as emerging after [[Artificial General Intelligence]] becomes capable of improving its own design.

The ethical concern is not simply that such a system would be malicious. A highly capable system could pursue an apparently harmless objective in ways that destroy things people value when the objective does not capture those values. This possibility motivates the [[AI Control Problem]] and [[AI Existential Risk]], although focusing exclusively on it can pull policy away from present and near-term harms.

2342.title: Summary Statistic
2342.heading: Summary Statistic
2342.content:
A summary statistic reduces a distribution to a numerical feature such as its count, mean, standard deviation, median, range, skewness, or standard error. Different measures describe different aspects of center, spread, and shape.

No single statistic fully describes a variable. Means and standard deviations can be misleading for strongly skewed data, so they should be read alongside [[Quantile|quantiles]] and visualizations such as histograms or box plots.

2344.title: Succinct Constraint

2345.title: Succinct Constraint
2345.heading: Succinct Constraint
2345.content:
A succinct constraint lets eligible items be selected directly before candidate generation. Conditions such as an item's category or value belonging to a specified range can reduce the transaction representation and the pattern search space immediately.

This property is valuable in distributed mining because it avoids communicating and processing items that cannot appear in a valid result.

2347.title: Subspace Search Space
2347.heading: Document

2348.sourceSearchName: subspace search space subspace search space
2348.title: Subspace Search Space
2348.heading: Subspace Search Space
2348.content:
With d attributes, the number of nonempty axis-parallel subspaces is exponential in d. If orientations are also allowed, candidate projections form a continuous and even larger search space.

Pruning, randomized search, monotonicity, local modeling, and integrated partitioning make the problem tractable. These approximations trade exhaustive coverage for speed, so evaluation should report stability and redundant or missed views.

2349.title: Subspace Search Space

2351.title: Substitution
2351.heading: Substitution
2351.content:
Substitution replaces a variable with an equivalent value or expression. It is the central step in [[Expression Evaluation]] and [[Equation Verification]]. Every occurrence governed by the assignment must be replaced consistently.

Grouping protects structure during replacement. If (x=-2), substituting into (x^2) gives ((-2)^2=4), not (-2^2=-4). An expression may also be substituted for a variable, allowing a general identity to generate a related one; replacing (b) by (-b) in the square-of-a-sum identity produces the square-of-a-difference identity.

2353.sourceSearchName: successive over relaxation successive over relaxation
2353.title: Successive Over-Relaxation
2353.heading: Document

2354.sourceSearchName: successive over relaxation successive over relaxation
2354.title: Successive Over-Relaxation
2354.heading: Successive Over-Relaxation
2354.content:
Successive over-relaxation modifies the [[Gauss-Seidel Method]] by blending the old component with its newly computed value using a relaxation factor $\omega$.

When $1<\omega<2$, over-relaxation may accelerate an already convergent system. Values $0<\omega<1$ under-relax the update and can stabilize some systems that otherwise diverge.

2357.sourceSearchName: subspace density clustering subspace density clustering
2357.title: Subspace Density Clustering
2357.heading: Subspace Density Clustering
2357.content:
Subspace density clustering searches for dense connected regions within selected subsets of dimensions. It addresses data in which a group is coherent only when irrelevant attributes are ignored.

The method must explore both spatial connectivity and a combinatorial feature space. Density monotonicity and pruning can reduce that search, but reported clusters may overlap in objects or dimensions and require redundancy control.

2360.heading: Subspace Cluster Representation
2360.content:
SubspaceCluster extends CenterCluster with a real-valued vector of dimension weights. Each weight expresses how strongly an attribute contributes to the formation or compactness of that particular cluster.

Per-cluster weights allow different groups to occupy different projected spaces while retaining an ordinary center and record collection. The vector length and ordering must match the shared schema.

2363.sourceSearchName: subscription based pricing subscription based pricing
2363.title: Subscription-Based Pricing
2363.heading: Subscription-Based Pricing
2363.content:
Subscription-based pricing gives access to a service for a recurring charge, usually independent of how fully the consumer uses the allocated capability. The agreement may include a minimum term or a notice period before cancellation.

The model makes spending predictable but can leave paid capacity unused. It can be applied at any service abstraction or deployment model when the access period is a more useful unit than individual resource consumption.

For an online game, a subscription creates a continuing obligation to provide reliable access, support, updates, and an experience worth the next payment. It suits ongoing worlds and services better than short, self-contained experiences, and some players resist paying repeatedly for continued access.

Status: #baby

Tags: [[Set Relations and Algebraic Foundations]] · [[Set Theory and Relations]]

2366.title: Subset
2366.heading: Subset
2366.content:
A subset is a set whose every element belongs to another set. The notation A ⊆ B allows equality, while a proper subset excludes equality.

Subsets become algebraic substructures only when they also preserve the operations of the larger structure.

The empty set is a subset of every set because an implication beginning with membership in the empty set can have no counterexample. The family of all subsets of A forms its [[Power Set]].

2368.title: Subset Construction
2368.heading: Document
2368.content:
2026-09-16 22:54

Status: #baby

Tags: [[Regular Languages and Finite Automata]]

2369.title: Subset Construction
2369.heading: Subset Construction
2369.content:
Subset construction converts a [[Nondeterministic Finite-State Automaton]] into a deterministic one by making each DFA state represent a set of NFA states reachable after the same input. Transitions collect every state reachable from the represented set, including those reached through ε-transitions.

The DFA start state is the NFA start state's ε-closure, and a set-state is accepting when it contains any NFA accepting state. The construction proves that nondeterministic and [[Deterministic Finite-State Automaton|deterministic finite automata]] recognize the same languages.

2372.title: Subring
2372.heading: Subring
2372.content:
A subring is a subset that remains a ring under the operations inherited from a larger ring. It must be closed under subtraction and multiplication and, under the book's convention, contain the same multiplicative identity.

A subring retains the ambient arithmetic without requiring the absorption property of an ideal.

2374.title: Subproject Dependency
2374.heading: Document
2374.content:
2026-09-06 22:42

Status: #baby

Tags: [[Big Data Project Value Management]]

2375.title: Subproject Dependency
2375.heading: Subproject Dependency
2375.content:
A subproject dependency requires one component or result to exist before another component can begin or deliver value. Dependencies restrict the rollout sequences available to a project portfolio.

Modeling them explicitly prevents a financially attractive but impossible order and reveals enabling work whose value is realized mainly through the downstream options it creates.

2377.sourceSearchName: subprogram call and return subprogram call and return
2377.title: Subprogram Call and Return
2377.heading: Document

2378.sourceSearchName: subprogram call and return subprogram call and return
2378.title: Subprogram Call and Return
2378.heading: Subprogram Call and Return
2378.content:
A call instruction transfers control to reusable code while saving enough information to resume the caller afterward. A return restores that saved continuation, allowing one subprogram to be invoked from many places.

Hardware support for call and return made functions, procedures, and libraries efficient building blocks. It enabled programs to be organized around reusable operations instead of repeated instruction sequences.

2379.sourceSearchName: subprogram call and return subprogram call and return
2379.title: Subprogram Call and Return
2379.heading: References

2380.title: Submodule
2380.heading: Document
2380.content:

Status: #baby

Tags: [[Module Structure and Exact Sequences]]

2381.title: Submodule
2381.heading: Submodule
2381.content:
A submodule N of an R-module M is a subset closed under addition and multiplication by scalars from R. Equivalently, it contains every R-linear combination of its elements.

An [[Ideal]] is precisely a submodule of a ring viewed as a module over itself. A submodule can be divided out to form a [[Quotient Module]] and can appear as the kernel or image in an exact sequence.

2384.title: Subjective Probability
2384.heading: Subjective Probability
2384.content:
Subjective probability represents the state of knowledge of a reasoner about a proposition or variable. A distribution is conditioned on preliminary knowledge, so two reasoners with different information can rationally assign different probabilities.

Subjective does not mean arbitrary. Assignments and updates must follow the probability rules consistently, and disagreement with observations can reveal that the preliminary knowledge or model structure should be revised.

2387.title: Subgroup
2387.heading: Subgroup
2387.content:
A subgroup is a subset of a group that is itself a group under the restricted operation. It shares the ambient identity and the inverse of each of its elements.

Subgroups capture internal symmetry and supply the pieces used to form cosets and quotient groups.

2390.title: Subgroup Test
2390.heading: Subgroup Test
2390.content:
The subgroup test verifies a nonempty subset H by checking that ab⁻¹ lies in H whenever a and b lie in H. This combines closure and inverse requirements into one condition.

For finite nonempty subsets, closure under the operation alone is sufficient.

2392.sourceSearchName: stylized augmented reality stylized augmented reality
2392.title: Stylized Augmented Reality
2392.heading: Document

2393.sourceSearchName: stylized augmented reality stylized augmented reality
2393.title: Stylized Augmented Reality
2393.heading: Stylized Augmented Reality
2393.content:
Stylized augmented reality gives real and virtual imagery a shared artistic treatment instead of pursuing photographic realism. The camera image may be transformed into a drawn, painted, or otherwise simplified representation while generated objects use compatible rendering.

A common style can hide small photometric differences and communicate intentional visual meaning. Geometric registration and temporal consistency still matter, because a coherent style does not correct content that slides or flickers relative to the world.

2394.sourceSearchName: stylized augmented reality stylized augmented reality
2394.title: Stylized Augmented Reality
2394.heading: References

2396.title: STTDF Object
2396.heading: STTDF Object
2396.content: An `STTDF` object represents a simple [[Spatial Trajectory]] together with attributes recorded along it. Locations are paired with ordered times so the structure describes movement rather than an independent grid of places and dates. Subsetting must preserve that pairing. A mapped path can show where the entity traveled, while temporal or attribute displays are needed to explain how its measurements changed along the route.

2399.title: Sturm Sequence
2399.heading: Sturm Sequence
2399.content:
A Sturm sequence is a recurrence of polynomials used to count how many eigenvalues of a symmetric tridiagonal matrix lie below a chosen value.

Comparing sign variations brackets eigenvalues and supports interval refinement. It locates individual eigenvalues without first forming all roots of a [[Characteristic Polynomial]].

2401.sourceSearchName: student t test student t test
2401.title: Student t-Test
2401.heading: Document

2026-09-06 18:44

Status: #baby

Tags: [[Descriptive Health Statistics]] · [[Statistical Inference and Resampling]]

2402.sourceSearchName: student t test student t test
2402.title: Student t-Test
2402.heading: Student t-Test
2402.content:
A two-sample Student t-test compares the means of a continuous variable between two independent groups. Its equal-variance form pools the group variances and evaluates the standardized mean difference against a t distribution.

The result should include group means, the t statistic, degrees of freedom, a confidence interval for the difference, and a p-value. If equal variance is doubtful, the [[Welch t-Test]] uses a different standard error and degrees-of-freedom calculation.

The source constructs the test from the observed mean difference and its estimated standard error before using R's `t.test` function. It emphasizes that the t-distribution gives an exact small-sample result only when the underlying population is adequately approximated by a normal distribution.

2403.sourceSearchName: student t test student t test
2403.title: Student t-Test
2403.heading: References

2405.title: STSDF Object
2405.heading: STSDF Object
2405.content: An `STSDF` object attaches attribute data to a [[Sparse Space-Time Grid]]. It stores only observed feature-time combinations while referring to spatial and temporal indexes that define the larger lattice. This representation is useful when observations share known locations and times but many crossings are absent. Methods can subset its spatial, temporal, or variable dimensions without first expanding it into a full grid.

2408.title: Structure Sheaf
2408.heading: Structure Sheaf
2408.content:
The structure sheaf O_X on X = Spec(A) assigns the localization A_f to each basic open set where f does not vanish. Restriction maps are the corresponding localization homomorphisms.

Its [[Sheaf Stalk]] at a prime p is A_p, a [[Local Ring]]. The pair (Spec(A),O_X) is an [[Affine Scheme]] and carries both the topology of prime ideals and their local algebra.

2410.sourceSearchName: structural symmetry reduction structural symmetry reduction
2410.title: Structural Symmetry Reduction
2410.heading: Document

2411.sourceSearchName: structural symmetry reduction structural symmetry reduction
2411.title: Structural Symmetry Reduction
2411.heading: Structural Symmetry Reduction
2411.content:
Structural symmetry reduction models only a repeated portion of a body when geometry, material, and loading are symmetric. Appropriate displacement constraints on the symmetry lines reproduce the omitted portions.

A plate with a centered hole and symmetric tension can be reduced to one quarter of the full domain. The reduction lowers computational cost while retaining the local stress field when boundary conditions are applied correctly.

2412.sourceSearchName: structural symmetry reduction structural symmetry reduction
2412.title: Structural Symmetry Reduction
2412.heading: References

2413.sourceSearchName: structural text representation structural text representation
2413.title: Structural Text Representation
2413.heading: Document

2414.sourceSearchName: structural text representation structural text representation
2414.title: Structural Text Representation
2414.heading: Structural Text Representation
2414.content:
A structural text representation describes syntactic or semantic relationships among words, phrases, and sentences. Parse-derived constructions can capture sentence organization that a [[Bag-of-Words Representation]] discards.

These features are useful when style, grammatical competence, authorship, or semantic roles matter. Their greater linguistic depth usually brings language dependence, parsing error, and computational cost, so shallow representations may remain preferable for robust topic-oriented tasks.

2415.sourceSearchName: structural text representation structural text representation
2415.title: Structural Text Representation
2415.heading: References

2416.sourceSearchName: structural mass matrix structural mass matrix
2416.title: Structural Mass Matrix
2416.heading: Document

2417.sourceSearchName: structural mass matrix structural mass matrix
2417.title: Structural Mass Matrix
2417.heading: Structural Mass Matrix
2417.content:
A structural mass matrix distributes element mass among nodal degrees of freedom so inertia can enter the finite element equations. Its coefficients depend on density, geometry, element length, and interpolation functions.

Element mass matrices are assembled using the same local-to-global mapping as stiffness matrices. In free vibration, the global mass matrix is multiplied by squared frequency in the generalized eigenvalue problem.

2418.sourceSearchName: structural mass matrix structural mass matrix
2418.title: Structural Mass Matrix
2418.heading: References

2419.title: Structural Identification
2419.heading: Document
2419.content:
2026-09-06 21:47

Status: #baby

Tags: [[Bayesian Parameter and Structure Learning]]

2420.title: Structural Identification
2420.heading: Structural Identification
2420.content:
Structural identification learns aspects of a probabilistic model's decomposition from data. Instead of assuming every conditional dependency in advance, it compares candidate factorizations or graph structures.

Learned structure can reveal a compact representation that supports more efficient inference. It does not automatically establish causation, because equivalent dependencies and unmodeled variables may explain the same observations.

2423.title: Structural Dynamics
2423.heading: Structural Dynamics
2423.content:
Structural dynamics studies systems with mass and components capable of relative motion. Loads and inertia make displacement vary with time, so stiffness alone is insufficient to describe the response.

Finite element dynamic models add mass and, when needed, damping matrices to the assembled stiffness system. Modal, harmonic, and transient analyses answer different questions about the resulting motion.

2425.title: StringBuilder
2425.heading: Document
2425.content:
2026-09-08 21:16

Status: #baby

Tags: [[.NET Core Data Types and Collections]]

2426.title: StringBuilder
2426.heading: StringBuilder
2426.content:
`StringBuilder` accumulates changing text in a mutable buffer. Appending, inserting, or replacing content can reuse its storage instead of creating a new immutable string after every operation.

The builder is most useful for repeated modifications in loops or large generated output. Once construction is complete, converting it to a string produces the immutable value expected by ordinary text APIs. Simple interpolation or a few concatenations usually remain clearer for small cases.

2428.sourceSearchName: structural damping matrix structural damping matrix
2428.title: Structural Damping Matrix
2428.heading: Document

2429.sourceSearchName: structural damping matrix structural damping matrix
2429.title: Structural Damping Matrix
2429.heading: Structural Damping Matrix
2429.content:
A structural damping matrix represents mechanisms that dissipate vibrational energy and oppose motion. It contributes a force proportional to nodal velocity in the standard linear dynamic equation.

The primer identifies damping as an additional matrix needed beyond stiffness and mass for general vibration analysis. Its presence limits resonance and governs decay in transient motion.

2430.sourceSearchName: structural damping matrix structural damping matrix
2430.title: Structural Damping Matrix
2430.heading: References

2432.title: Structural Coupling
2432.heading: Structural Coupling
2432.content:
Structural coupling occurs when recurrent interactions mold two or more systems into congruent structures. The systems remain distinct but adapt in response to one another as parts of a larger system.

A game and player become structurally coupled as the player learns the [[Game Model]] and the game responds to the player's actions. This relationship supports engagement when their models remain close enough for prediction without eliminating uncertainty.

2434.sourceSearchName: strongly connected attribute values strongly connected attribute values
2434.title: Strongly Connected Attribute Values
2434.heading: Document

2435.sourceSearchName: strongly connected attribute values strongly connected attribute values
2435.title: Strongly Connected Attribute Values
2435.heading: Strongly Connected Attribute Values
2435.content:
Two categorical values from different attributes are strongly connected when their observed co-occurrence exceeds a multiple of the support expected under independence. Sets are strongly connected when all relevant cross-pairs meet that condition.

CACTUS uses maximal strongly connected sets with sufficient support as the basis for cluster projections and candidates.

2437.title: Strong Induction

2438.title: Strong Induction
2438.heading: Strong Induction
2438.content:
Strong induction proves P(k + 1) under the assumption that every earlier case P(0), P(1), …, P(k) is true. With a suitable base case, this establishes P(n) for every natural number.

The stronger induction hypothesis is natural when the next object is assembled from components of several smaller sizes, as in prime factorizations or recursively structured trees. It has the same proving power as ordinary [[Mathematical Induction]].

2441.heading: Strong Computational View of Nature
2441.content:
The strong computational view claims that the universe and its living beings are literally computational systems. Space, time, matter, and thought would all arise from underlying information processing rather than merely being modeled that way.

The claim is philosophically ambitious and empirically speculative. Its attraction reflects a recurring habit of interpreting the world through the dominant technology of an era.

2444.content:
A string text representation treats a document as an encoded sequence of characters. Byte sequences interpreted through standards such as UTF-8 can represent written symbols from many languages without first assuming words, grammar, or meaning.

This shallow form supports operations such as approximate matching, spelling correction, plagiarism alignment, and spam similarity. It is general but poorly suited to semantic tasks because character sequence alone does not expose word identity or higher linguistic structure.

2447.title: String
2447.heading: String
2447.content:
A string is a finite sequence of symbols from an [[Alphabet]]. Its length counts symbols, concatenation appends one sequence to another, and reversal lists the same symbols in the opposite order.

String equality requires both equal length and the same symbol in every position. Concatenation is associative but generally not commutative, and the [[Empty String]] serves as its identity.

2450.title: String Sorting
2450.heading: String Sorting
2450.content:
String sorting treats a key as a sequence of symbols such as characters or digits. The symbols must have an order, allowing complete strings to be ordered lexicographically or processed one position at a time.

[[Radix Sort]] is called a string-sorting method because it distributes items by individual key positions. A numerical key such as 123 is handled as the ordered symbols 1, 2, and 3 rather than as one indivisible number.

An imported Blender asset must map its textures and material parameters into that real-time representation. Similar PBR terminology does not guarantee identical appearance, so lighting, color space, normals, and roughness should be checked in the target renderer.

2459.heading: Strict Diagonal Dominance
2459.content:
A square matrix is strictly diagonally dominant when, in every row, the absolute diagonal entry is greater than the sum of the absolute values of all other entries in that row.

This structural condition guarantees nonsingularity and supplies a useful sufficient condition for convergence of the [[Jacobi Method]] and [[Gauss-Seidel Method]]. It is sufficient, not necessary: some nondominant systems also converge.

2462.content:
A stress concentration factor is the ratio of maximum local stress to a nominal reference stress. Holes and other geometric discontinuities raise local stress above the value predicted from net or gross section averages.

Analytical factors offer a benchmark for finite element results. Accurate numerical estimation requires a mesh fine enough around the discontinuity to resolve the steep gradient.

2465.heading: Stress-Strain Curve
2465.content: A stress-strain curve plots force per unit area against fractional deformation. Its initial linear gradient is [[Young's Modulus]]. The end of proportional behavior, elastic limit, yield region, ultimate tensile stress, and fracture point distinguish stiffness, recoverability, strength, and ductility. The curve describes material behavior independently of the specimen's original dimensions.

`StreamReader` and `StreamWriter` wrap a .NET stream with text-oriented reading and writing. They translate between characters and bytes using an encoding and offer operations such as line-based reads and writes.

2471.title: Streamline
2471.heading: Streamline
2471.content:
A streamline is a curve whose tangent at every point aligns with the instantaneous local velocity vector. In steady flow, the streamline pattern does not change with time and traces particle trajectories.

Stream functions label streamlines by constant values in two-dimensional incompressible flow. Around an impermeable body, the surface itself becomes a streamline because normal velocity is zero.

2474.title: Streamline Map
2474.heading: Streamline Map
2474.content: A streamline map draws curves that are tangent to a [[Vector Field Map]] at each point. The curves reveal continuous flow structure, convergence, and circulation more readily than isolated arrows. Their spacing and seeds are graphical choices rather than measurements, and a streamline does not necessarily trace the path of a physical particle through a changing field. Direction cues and a magnitude encoding may be added when shape alone is insufficient.

2477.sourceSearchName: streaming recommender system streaming recommender system
2477.title: Streaming Recommender System
2477.heading: Streaming Recommender System
2477.content:
A streaming recommender system updates or produces recommendations from interactions that arrive continuously. It must respond to changing interests and new items without rebuilding the entire model after every event.

Streaming design balances freshness against computation and stability. Online updates, bounded state, and time-sensitive evaluation become important when the usefulness of a preference signal decays quickly.

2480.title: Streaming Machine Learning
2480.heading: Streaming Machine Learning
2480.content:
Streaming machine learning updates a model or produces predictions from a continuing sequence without repeatedly retraining from a complete stored dataset. Incremental algorithms use bounded state and can adapt as conditions change.

They must detect concept drift, control the influence of stale data, and evaluate accuracy when labels arrive late or only for a subset of events.

2483.title: Streaming Locally Linear Embedding
2483.heading: Streaming Locally Linear Embedding
2483.content:
Streaming Locally Linear Embedding extends neighborhood-preserving manifold learning to arriving data. It incrementally places new observations using local reconstruction relationships instead of rebuilding the entire embedding.

The approach preserves nearby geometry when neighborhoods remain informative. A changing manifold, insufficient stored landmarks, or expensive neighbor search can weaken both accuracy and scalability.

2486.sourceSearchName: streaming feature engineering streaming feature engineering
2486.title: Streaming Feature Engineering
2486.heading: Streaming Feature Engineering
2486.content:
Streaming feature engineering adapts representation construction to data that cannot be stored and revisited as a fixed batch. Algorithms must update features in one pass, under limited memory, while the stream's length and future content remain unknown.

The term covers both arriving observations and arriving dimensions. These settings demand incremental statistics, compact sketches, bounded computation, and decisions that remain useful as the available data or feature space changes.

2489.sourceSearchName: streaming kernel learning streaming kernel learning
2489.title: Streaming Kernel Learning
2489.heading: Streaming Kernel Learning
2489.content:
Streaming kernel learning constructs or updates nonlinear feature mappings as data arrive. Budgeted bases, approximations, or incremental kernel matrices keep computation from growing without bound.

The kernel supplies expressive similarity features, but an unrestricted set of support points is incompatible with long streams. Budget maintenance therefore balances fidelity to the nonlinear structure against fixed memory and update time.

2492.title: Streaming Feature Setting
2492.heading: Streaming Feature Setting
2492.content:
A streaming feature setting presents new dimensions sequentially for a collection of observations. The learner must decide how to use or retain each feature without knowing the complete feature space in advance.

This differs from an ordinary data stream because variables, rather than cases, are the arriving objects. Irreversible decisions, feature order, redundancy, and the cost of storing accepted dimensions shape the algorithm.

2495.sourceSearchName: streaming instance setting streaming instance setting
2495.title: Streaming Instance Setting
2495.heading: Streaming Instance Setting
2495.content:
A streaming instance setting presents new observations over time while the set of measured variables is comparatively stable. Feature extractors update their state from each instance rather than repeatedly processing the complete history.

Online dimension reduction and latent-variable methods operate in this regime. Their challenge is to approximate batch representations with limited memory while remaining responsive to changes in the data distribution.

2498.sourceSearchName: streaming feature selection streaming feature selection
2498.title: Streaming Feature Selection
2498.heading: Streaming Feature Selection
2498.content:
Streaming feature selection decides whether to retain each variable as features arrive over time and the complete feature space is not available in advance. The method must evaluate a new feature against the subset already accepted.

This setting reverses the familiar data-stream problem: observations may be fixed while dimensions arrive sequentially. Memory limits and the inability to revisit rejected variables make redundancy control, statistical error control, and stable online decisions central concerns.

The broader streaming literature also evaluates selectors by stability, retained feature count, and their ability to handle heterogeneous or interacting dimensions. Online relevance must be assessed against features already accepted, not in isolation.

2501.title: Streamgraph
2501.heading: Streamgraph
2501.content: A streamgraph represents additive time-series components as flowing colored bands arranged around a varying baseline. Like a [[ThemeRiver]], it emphasizes changes in composition and the overall shape of the total. The organic layout can make emergence and decline easy to notice, but position changes and curved boundaries impede precise comparison. It should therefore use a restrained qualitative palette and provide labels or interaction when individual components must be identified.

2503.sourceSearchName: stream support vector classification stream support vector classification
2503.title: Stream Support Vector Classification
2503.heading: Document

2504.sourceSearchName: stream support vector classification stream support vector classification
2504.title: Stream Support Vector Classification
2504.heading: Stream Support Vector Classification
2504.content:
Stream support vector classification updates a margin-based decision boundary as cases arrive rather than solving a batch optimization problem over the full dataset. Online steps adjust the current weight vector from individual observations or small batches.

The method must balance rapid updates with the stability of the margin. Nonstationary data may require forgetting or time-sensitive weights so that obsolete support from an earlier concept does not dominate current predictions.

2505.sourceSearchName: stream support vector classification stream support vector classification
2505.title: Stream Support Vector Classification
2505.heading: References

2506.sourceSearchName: stream rule based classification stream rule based classification
2506.title: Stream Rule-Based Classification
2506.heading: Document

2507.sourceSearchName: stream rule based classification stream rule based classification
2507.title: Stream Rule-Based Classification
2507.heading: Stream Rule-Based Classification
2507.content:
Stream rule-based classification maintains if-then conditions from incrementally updated coverage and class statistics. Rules can be added, specialized, retired, or reweighted as new labeled cases arrive.

Unlike a fixed batch rule set, the model must represent both current evidence and change over time. Local rule updates can adapt a portion of the feature space without discarding conditions that remain useful elsewhere.

2508.sourceSearchName: stream rule based classification stream rule based classification
2508.title: Stream Rule-Based Classification
2508.heading: References

2509.sourceSearchName: stream neural network classification stream neural network classification
2509.title: Stream Neural Network Classification
2509.heading: Document

2510.sourceSearchName: stream neural network classification stream neural network classification
2510.title: Stream Neural Network Classification
2510.heading: Stream Neural Network Classification
2510.content:
Stream neural network classification applies incremental gradient updates to a network as labeled observations become available. Each update changes a nonlinear boundary without requiring a complete retraining pass.

The learning rate and memory mechanism determine how quickly the network responds to changing distributions. Rehearsal, decay, or ensembles can reduce catastrophic replacement of older but still relevant patterns.

2513.title: Stream Nearest Neighbor Classification
2513.heading: Stream Nearest Neighbor Classification
2513.content:
Stream nearest-neighbor classification predicts from a maintained sample of recent or representative labeled observations. Because storing every case violates bounded-memory requirements, the learner must discard, summarize, or selectively retain instances.

The retention policy defines the model's temporal memory. Keeping recent cases aids adaptation, while preserving rare or boundary cases protects predictive coverage that a simple sliding window could erase.

2516.title: Stream Function
2516.heading: Stream Function
2516.content:
A stream function is a scalar representation of two-dimensional incompressible flow whose derivatives give orthogonal velocity components. Curves of constant stream function are streamlines.

It automatically satisfies mass conservation in the plane. The choice between stream function and velocity potential depends on geometry and which boundary conditions are simpler to express.

2518.sourceSearchName: stream ensemble classification stream ensemble classification
2518.title: Stream Ensemble Classification
2518.heading: Document

2519.sourceSearchName: stream ensemble classification stream ensemble classification
2519.title: Stream Ensemble Classification
2519.heading: Stream Ensemble Classification
2519.content:
Stream ensemble classification combines incrementally trained base models and changes their weights or membership according to recent performance. Components trained during different periods provide alternative views of an evolving distribution.

Replacing weak members allows adaptation without rebuilding the entire classifier at once. Diversity remains important: an ensemble of models that fail on the same drift offers little protection beyond a single learner.

2520.sourceSearchName: stream ensemble classification stream ensemble classification
2520.title: Stream Ensemble Classification
2520.heading: References

2521.sourceSearchName: stream decision tree classification stream decision tree classification
2521.title: Stream Decision Tree Classification
2521.heading: Document

2522.sourceSearchName: stream decision tree classification stream decision tree classification
2522.title: Stream Decision Tree Classification
2522.heading: Stream Decision Tree Classification
2522.content:
Stream decision tree classification selects splits from incremental statistics rather than repeatedly storing and sorting all past observations. A split is committed when accumulated evidence makes the best candidate sufficiently better than alternatives.

This permits bounded-memory learning and continuous prediction. Because an early split may later become obsolete, evolving streams also require monitoring, alternate subtrees, or rebuilding strategies to respond to concept drift.

2525.heading: STREAM Clustering Algorithm

STREAM processes a large sequence in manageable batches. Each batch is clustered locally, its centers are retained as weighted representatives, and those representatives are periodically reclustered to form the final solution.

The approach converts a memory-intensive problem into repeated clustering of bounded summaries. Approximation quality depends on how well weighted centers preserve the original geometry and on how errors accumulate across compression levels.

2528.title: Strategy Pattern
2528.heading: Strategy Pattern
2528.content:
The strategy pattern defines interchangeable algorithms behind one operation and chooses which one to apply at runtime. A caller can request an outcome without embedding a branch for every algorithm. The book also shows a functional version: a filtering operation accepts a `Func<T, bool>` criterion, so supplying a different predicate changes the selection strategy without adding another class.

Strategy turns a family of algorithms into interchangeable implementations of one abstraction. An object can receive the appropriate behavior through composition, avoiding an inheritance hierarchy that mixes independent behavioral dimensions.

2531.title: Stream Classification
2531.heading: Stream Classification
2531.content:
Stream classification predicts labels for observations that arrive continuously and often can be examined only once. A learner must update a bounded model without retaining the complete historical dataset.

The setting combines immediate prediction with incremental training. Its evaluation is temporal because the model used for a case should contain only evidence available before that case or label arrived.

2534.title: Strategy Game
2534.heading: Strategy Game
2534.content:
A strategy game emphasizes planning, resource use, positioning, and decisions whose consequences unfold over time. The player manages forces or systems to achieve objectives against an opponent or environment.

Good strategy preserves several viable approaches and provides enough information for plans to be formed and revised. Real-time and turn-based structures change the amount of time pressure without eliminating the need for strategic choice.

2536.sourceSearchName: storytelling preference in games storytelling preference in games
2536.title: Storytelling Preference in Games
2536.heading: Document

2537.sourceSearchName: storytelling preference in games storytelling preference in games
2537.title: Storytelling Preference in Games
2537.heading: Storytelling Preference in Games
2537.content:
Storytelling preference is the importance a player assigns to characters, plot, and dramatic context. Some players treat story as the main reason to continue, while others prefer games where social or mechanical activity needs little narrative support.

Genres differ in how naturally they use story. The design should integrate narrative with the intended play rather than adding it as an obligation that interrupts the player's preferred activity.

2538.sourceSearchName: storytelling preference in games storytelling preference in games
2538.title: Storytelling Preference in Games
2538.heading: References

2540.title: Story-Game
2540.heading: Story-Game
2540.content:
A story-game is a game in which choosing how an authored story proceeds is the primary verb. The player reads or observes a situation, selects from available responses, and follows the resulting [[Branching Story|branch]].

The form descends from gamebooks and can make unavailable options meaningful as well as available ones. Even when choices are constrained, they let players express preferences and search for the version of the story they want to experience.

2543.title: Story Splitting
2543.heading: Story Splitting
2543.content:
Story splitting divides an epic into Sprint-sized stories that each preserve a testable increment of value. Useful split dimensions include player progression, scenarios, conjunctions, acceptance conditions, and knowledge gained through research or prototyping.

Splitting by discipline creates components that may remain unusable until late integration. Vertical, value-oriented splits instead create earlier feedback about the whole experience.

2546.title: Story Point
2546.heading: Story Point
2546.content:
A story point is a team-specific unit for the relative size and complexity of a Product Backlog Item. It combines the effort, difficulty, and uncertainty perceived by the people who will do the work.

Story points are not hours and should not be compared across teams. Their planning value comes from relating a team's completed points to its own historical [[Velocity]].

2549.title: Story Mapping
2549.heading: Story Mapping
2549.content:
Story mapping arranges stories in two dimensions: a player or product narrative across one axis and priority or forecasted delivery slices across the other. A narrative backbone preserves why the pieces belong together while smaller stories fill planned increments beneath it.

The map gives a release a visible big picture that a one-dimensional backlog cannot. Teams can move stories, dependencies, and Sprint boundaries as the product emerges while retaining coherent player-facing goals.

2551.sourceSearchName: story as system story as system
2551.title: Story as System
2551.heading: Document

2552.sourceSearchName: story as system story as system
2552.title: Story as System
2552.heading: Story as System
2552.content:
Story as system conveys narrative meaning through the structure of a game's rules and the experience of acting within them. Resistance, available verbs, consequences, and recurring interactions can express what a situation feels like without relying only on words or images.

The designed system makes some actions important and others impossible, implicitly describing how its world works. Players discover that message by pushing into the rules and interpreting the responses they receive.

2553.sourceSearchName: story as system story as system
2553.title: Story as System
2553.heading: References

2554.sourceSearchName: story as exertion story as exertion
2554.title: Story as Exertion
2554.heading: Document

2555.sourceSearchName: story as exertion story as exertion
2555.title: Story as Exertion
2555.heading: Story as Exertion
2555.content:
Story as exertion makes progress through a narrative depend on the player's work within a game system. Quests, puzzles, or combat become the means by which the next authored event is reached.

Effort can strengthen attachment because the player has helped move the story forward. It can also turn play into a chore when repetitive or frustrating tasks become barriers and the story reward is more compelling than the process used to reach it.

2556.sourceSearchName: story as exertion story as exertion
2556.title: Story as Exertion
2556.heading: References

2557.sourceSearchName: stored program principle stored program principle
2557.title: Stored-Program Principle
2557.heading: Document

2558.sourceSearchName: stored program principle stored program principle
2558.title: Stored-Program Principle
2558.heading: Stored-Program Principle
2558.content:
The stored-program principle places instructions and data in a common high-speed memory. A processor can fetch both electronically, avoiding the mechanical or manual delays of tapes, cards, and plugboards.

Because instructions share the same representation as data, a program can generate, copy, or modify other programs. This principle enabled compilers and flexible general-purpose computing.
